#         fees[] vector<u64> }
# base:   rpc_access_response_base (credits, top_hash) :124-136
# METHOD NAME: the struct is COMMAND_RPC_GET_BASE_FEE_ESTIMATE but the json_rpc method -- and
#         therefore this file's name -- is `get_fee_estimate` (src/rpc/core_rpc_server.h:176).
# request: grace_blocks (:2257). fmonero ALWAYS sends 10, the FEE_ESTIMATE_GRACE_BLOCKS wallet2
#         itself uses (src/wallet/wallet2.cpp:123, applied at :8597), so the chips the Send screen
#         draws are the fees the build will charge. grace_blocks 0 returns a different fees[].
# `fee` IS fees[0], NOT a "normal" tier: since HF 15 on_get_base_fee_estimate ends
#         `res.fee = res.fees[0]` (src/rpc/core_rpc_server.cpp:3011-3012), i.e. the CHEAPEST level.
#         DESIGN.md §5 renders it as node.fee.per_byte_pico beside fees_pico and no code may treat it
#         as a default -- hence fee == fees[0] == 20000 here, and it must stay that way.
# fees[] has exactly four entries, in order, and they ARE the four priority levels 1..4
#         (wallet2::get_base_fee clamps priority 0 -> 1 and > 4 -> 4, decrements, and indexes this
#         array: src/wallet/wallet2.cpp:8584-8609). So --priority 0 and --priority 1 both land on
#         20000 -- the fact DESIGN.md §1b.4 spends a paragraph on.
# quantization_mask: KV_SERIALIZE_OPT default 1 (:2275); 10000 is the mainnet value since HF 15.
# VALUES are the worked example of DESIGN.md §5 verbatim, so §5's document and this fixture cannot
#         disagree: per_byte_pico 20000, fees_pico [20000, 80000, 320000, 4000000].
